external_spec_note: The indivisible-amount truncation is derivable purely from the four statements' own integer-division literals (4, 12/5, 9/2, 9) and ordinary integer-division semantics; no protocol/business convention needed.
finding_level_note: Four symmetric members of the same indivisible_amount finding in sendETHToTeam, one per fee-split leg: Member A (@During, line 140, transfer.arg[0] > 0) covers `_devWalletAddress.transfer(amount.div(4))`; Member B (line 141) covers `_marketingWalletAddress.transfer(amount.div(12).mul(5))`; Member C (line 142) covers `_dipWalletAddress.transfer(amount.div(9).mul(2))`; Member D (line 143) covers `_marketingWalletAddress2.transfer(amount.div(9))`. All four independently Expressible=Yes, same relation form/scope (each asserts the corresponding transfer's actual argument is nonzero), so a single unioned RQ2-A profile is reported (per the 29_H_08 precedent) rather than four separate breakdowns to sum. The debug scenario (amount=3) drives every one of the four integer divisions to 0 simultaneously, which is the point of the finding: small `amount` values make the whole four-way split indivisible, not just one leg.
case_notes: Ordinary Solidity/SafeMath integer-division truncation (division rounds toward zero) is load-bearing for all four members -- it is exactly why amount.div(4), amount.div(12).mul(5), amount.div(9).mul(2) and amount.div(9) can each independently collapse to 0 for small `amount`. Per Step 2 this is a generic, protocol-independent language-semantics fact, so it is recorded as a case note rather than counted under Additional functions.
